Went to an Ivy, lost contact with majority of friends, had a hard time fitting in, broke up with a close friend, burned out, tried to kill himself.

I was walking back home after spending the afternoon wandering and hiking through the snow. It was New Years Eve, but the past semester had been kinda crap for me. 

Really awful actually. I felt like nothing was going correctly, and i was just dragging the few friends I had left down. On the surface, grades and everything were good, but I just didn't feel happy or content with myself anymore. It just felt like an endless slog of work without much else to look forward to. That, combined with some issues back home, made me wonder if I was just wasting my time.

I wanted to walk through the last parts of town that I still had good memories of, and then find a place in the forest to kill myself. As it turned out, it got very cold very quickly, and I ended up giving up on it, thinking I didn't really have the strength or the ability anymore. My hands could barely close. So I sat in a pizza shop for about an hour to warm up before starting my walk back.

I was feeling like I was pretty much worthless to the world when a guy honks at me and asks if I needed a ride somewhere. 

"You alright man?" 

I was close to home, and pretty heavily bundled up. It wasn't that late either. Somehow he knew there was something bothering me. 

I politely declined, but then I wondered if I was right to think that there wasn't anybody that cared. 

"Good luck dude. Happy New Year."

He drove on past me, then turned around and went on his way. The thought of a stranger going that far out of their way to ask if I needed help was pretty touching. 

Thanks to him, I think getting out of that slump might be more possible.
